tasks.short: Arrange animal or egg sales with checked offers, agreed terms and a complete sale record.

steps.what: Retrieve available animals or eggs, buyer details and relevant sale records
Assess buyer requirements and the suitability and availability of animals or eggs
Discuss and agree sale terms and delivery arrangements with the buyer
Write the animal or egg sale confirmation and delivery particulars
Send the checked final sale confirmation to the buyer
Record the agreed sale, reserved stock and delivery arrangements

tasks.design: Configure stock and buyer views in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {CRM}, with a sale confirmation template in {DOCS}. Keep suitability and negotiation with the breeder, separately write and send the exact final confirmation through {EMAIL}, then record the sale arrangement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock facts, delivery particulars and agreed terms are repeatedly located and written.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views, confirmation headings and sale record fields can reduce supporting administration.
tasks.still_hard: Buyer suitability, animal condition and delivery commitments need judgement and agreement.
tasks.human_edge: Arrange a suitable sale and avoid promises that the animals, stock or delivery cannot support.

ambition.what: Prepare consistent sale information for another suitable institutional buyer.

tasks.altitude: Spend sale effort on suitability and dependable arrangements.

reach.task: Arrange the agreed animal or egg delivery
reach.learn: Use exact stock identity, timing and handling requirements.

evidence.claim: Native stock and buyer views, confirmation templates and sale fields could reduce supporting sale work; this is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: The task owns sale arrangement records and the confirmation, separately priced from negotiation. Physical delivery and later invoicing are separate activities.

The breeder produces animal or batch identity, quantity, buyer, price, delivery date and handling terms in s4, retaining 14 hours, then records the sale in s6 with eight retained hours. Missing stock identity or agreed terms require manual clarification.
Native views and headings come first. No software negotiates, decides buyer suitability or sends an unchecked commitment.
Actual buyer statements and the final confirmation are checked when communicated. Internal author saves have no separate approval stage or saving.
unknowns: Current stock visibility and variation in buyer delivery requirements.
research_questions: Can native confirmation headings save work when institutional buyers require bespoke handling and delivery terms?

already_counted.description: Write exact sale terms and delivery particulars.

incremental.description: Maintain stock views and confirmation headings.

approvals.approved_version: Each exact offer, price, stock commitment and delivery term is checked against current availability before agreement.
Exact final confirmation, animal or batch identities, quantities, price, delivery terms and buyer recipient; changes require a fresh send-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=89, gross=11; upkeep=3 gives net=8. Conservative case: unreliable stock views and bespoke buyer terms retain lookup and record entry, while confirmation writing retains 16 of 20 hours; R=96, net=1. Usable stock metadata with lookup 13, confirmation 15 and recording nine gives R=92, net=5. Suitability, negotiation and actual sending retain 55 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Exercise animals appropriately and separately record their response and any concerns.

steps.what: Check the animals' exercise instructions and recent condition notes
Assess animal condition and choose suitable exercise for the current circumstances
Prepare the animals, handling equipment and exercise area
Exercise animals and adapt the activity to their observed behaviour and condition
Check the animals after exercise and identify any condition concerns
Record the exercise completed, animal response and condition concerns

tasks.design: Configure linked animal exercise instructions and a compact condition note template in {DOCS}. Retain condition assessment, preparation, physical exercise and the post-exercise check; simplify only lookup and the separately priced existing care note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercise instructions and recurring care note headings require small repeated lookup and writing actions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document links and note headings can support those actions.
tasks.still_hard: Animal behaviour and condition require direct observation and appropriate handling.
tasks.human_edge: Notice distress or a changed condition and adapt the activity.
tasks.altitude: Keep attention on animal condition while simplifying a small amount of supporting writing.

reach.task: Review the animal's recent exercise response
reach.learn: Use the actual response and condition concerns rather than an assumed normal outcome.

evidence.claim: Native exercise instruction links and care note headings could save a small amount of supporting effort; physical exercise and condition assessment remain human.

assumptions: This scenario has an existing brief exercise condition note. If no note is currently made, do not add one for a saving or claim the note-writing benefit.

The breeder produces animal ID, exercise activity, duration, observed response and concern in s6 with four retained hours. Missing or ambiguous observations are manually checked; no model infers the animal's condition.
Native links and headings come first. No automated animal handling, activity decision or alert is proposed.
An ordinary internal author save is incidental, ungated and earns no separate saving. Physical care retains all 90 hours.
unknowns: Existing care note practice and frequency of changed exercise instructions.
research_questions: Do links and note headings save even a small amount of work under the farm's actual care record practice?

already_counted.description: Capture the exercise response and condition concern.

incremental.description: Keep exercise links and note headings current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 existing-note case: B=100, R=98, gross=2; upkeep=0.5 gives net=1.5. Conservative case: already familiar instructions give no lookup gain and bespoke concerns retain 4.5 of five note hours, R=99.5, net=0. Usable links retaining four lookup hours and 4.5 note hours give R=98.5, net=1. All condition checks, preparation and exercise retain 90 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain breeding event records and the linked semen-use ledger without repeated re-keying.

steps.what: Retrieve the animal identity and semen specimen or straw details
Capture the actual breeding event and specimens used
Enter and verify the animal breeding event and associated specimen usage
Update the semen-use and stock ledger from the verified breeding event
Reconcile semen specimens used against the animals bred and resolve mismatches
Save the corrected log in the same breeding record system

tasks.design: Configure a single breeding event entry in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the herd and semen records system, linked to the specimen-use ledger. Replace the baseline separate stock re-key in {SPREADSHEET} with a native linked update from the verified event, while retaining reconciliation and the ordinary same-system save.
tasks.previous_blocker: The animal breeding event and semen-use stock ledger are entered separately.
tasks.enabler_now: A native linked breeding event can update the associated semen stock record.
tasks.still_hard: Misidentified animals, straws or actual quantities require physical and record reconciliation.
tasks.human_edge: Confirm what breeding event actually occurred and which specimen was used.

ambition.what: Spot mismatches between breeding events and semen use sooner.

tasks.altitude: Maintain one traceable event rather than re-keying it into separate logs.

reach.task: Use breeding and semen stock records
reach.learn: Trace the animal event to the exact specimen and stock movement.

evidence.claim: CRV Dier records inseminations and natural services and updates semen stock when an insemination is entered.

assumptions: The E1 baseline scenario has an animal event record plus a separately re-keyed semen-use stock spreadsheet. If the existing system already links both, the 20-hour duplicate-entry benefit does not apply.

The breeder produces animal ID, event date, service type, donor or straw ID, canister and quantity in s2, retaining 20 hours. Verification and the exact stock transaction check are counted in s3's 20 retained hours. Missing or conflicting identities stop the update and require manual resolution.
The stock update is a distinct ledger transaction replacing real duplicate entry, not a same-system author save. Its gate is the checked event and stock quantity in s3, not a new approval meeting.
Try native linked stock settings first. The one-hour ordinary corrected-log save retains all its time and has no self-approval gate.
unknowns: Whether stock is already linked and how reliably straws and animals are identified.
research_questions: Does a native linked event remove actual duplicate stock entry after mismatch reconciliation?

already_counted.description: Verify the breeding event and exact specimen-use transaction.

incremental.description: Maintain specimen identifiers and linked stock reconciliation.

approvals.approved_version: Exact verified event, animal, donor or straw, canister, use quantity and destination stock ledger; any change requires renewed s3 checking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 duplicate-entry case: B=100, R=67, gross=33; upkeep=5 gives net=28. Conservative case: incomplete specimen IDs retain all lookup, capture and event-entry work plus 11 of 20 stock-entry hours, R=91, net=4. Reliable IDs with lookup 13, capture 22, event entry 22 and stock entry five, plus 15 reconciliation and save hours, give R=77, net=18. If stock entry is already linked, assess a different baseline and claim no duplicate-entry benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Package semen, prepare traceable labels and separately record collection and quality particulars.

steps.what: Verify semen specimen identity and the date, source, quality and concentration evidence
Record semen packaging identity, date, source, quality and concentration fields
Package the semen specimen using the applicable handling procedure
Generate and print the semen label from the captured specimen fields
Match and attach the label to the correct packaged semen specimen
Check the package label against the specimen record and correct discrepancies

tasks.design: Configure specimen fields in {OPS_SYSTEM} and a native label template in {OTHER}, the label printing system. Keep specimen verification, packaging, label matching and final checks with the breeder; separately record particulars and generate the draft label from them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specimen particulars are repeatedly copied into a record and a handwritten or separately composed label.
tasks.enabler_now: A native label template can reuse captured specimen fields.
tasks.still_hard: The physical specimen, package and label must remain correctly matched.
tasks.human_edge: Detect a wrong source, quality value or package identity before the material is used.
tasks.altitude: Improve physical and record traceability while reducing repeat label composition.

reach.learn: Match label details with the actual specimen record.

evidence.claim: The digest describes semen traceability records and labelled collection and donor identifiers; it supports preserving those particulars, not a measured packaging saving.
Native specimen fields and label printing could reduce repeated record and label composition; the saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: OTHER means the label printing system. This task owns packaging particulars and physical labelling; the later breeding-use log is a separate event, without repeated capture credit.

The breeder produces specimen ID, date, donor or source, quality result, concentration and package identity in s2, retaining 16 hours. Source laboratory results already contain quality and concentration; verification of their applicability is counted in s1. Missing values stop label generation and require manual resolution.
The printed label remains a draft until physically matched and checked in s5 and s6. No release, external send or automated quality verdict is proposed.
Native record and label settings come first. Ordinary author saves have no extra approval stage or saving.
unknowns: Current printer support and reliability of source quality metadata.
research_questions: Does field-based printing reduce total label work after physical package matching and correction?

already_counted.description: Capture and correct specimen label fields.

incremental.description: Maintain label layouts and specimen field mappings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=81, gross=19; upkeep=4 gives net=15. Conservative case: variable source metadata retains all 20 capture hours and nine of 15 label hours for manual correction, R=94, net=2. Compatible fields with capture 18 and label correction three give R=86, net=10. Verification, physical packaging, label matching and final checks retain 65 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep animal care, breeding identity and sale judgement human while improving complete records and labels.
reach: Connect actual animals and specimens with traceable breeding logs, packages and sale commitments.
skills_to_grow: Configure native records and label layouts
Check exact sale and stock transactions
role.ambitious_version: An animal breeder who cares for animals directly and keeps clear, reliable breeding, specimen and sale records with less repeated entry.
